# Docs hierarchy unit fixture leaks its HighlightJS stub

## Context
Emmy found a deterministic same-worker failure while validating the unit-family runner (`#20347`). Sophie independently reproduced it on `708ff81d90`: 9 passed, 1 failed, 2 did not run.

## The Problem
After the Docs hierarchy spec runs, importing the real HighlightJS addon throws `Namespace collision in unitTestMode for Neo.main.addon.HighlightJS`. Reproducer:
```sh
CI=true NEO_TEST_SKIP_CI=true npx playwright test -c test/playwright/playwright.config.unit.mjs test/playwright/unit/apps/docs/view/classdetails/HierarchyTreeList.spec.mjs test/playwright/unit/main/addon/HighlightJS.spec.mjs --workers=1 --retries=0
```

## The Architectural Reality
`withDocs()` in `test/playwright/unit/apps/docs/view/classdetails/HierarchyTreeList.spec.mjs:44` installs a plain namespace stub for MembersList. Its finally block destroys components and the collection but leaves the stub behind. `src/Neo.mjs:905` correctly rejects that non-singleton object when the real addon registers. The test fixture owns this temporary state; the engine guard and addon are correct.

## The Fix
Restore the prior HighlightJS property after the fixture finishes, including callback failure, or remove it when the fixture introduced it. Keep cleanup inside the existing spec and preserve any preexisting addon. No new public contract or runtime behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The two specs above pass together in one worker with zero retries.
- [ ] The fixture restores the prior namespace property on success and callback rejection.
- [ ] Existing hierarchy/member assertions remain intact.

## Out of Scope
Production addon changes, weakening namespace collision detection, CI orchestration, and broader Docs navigation.

## Avoided Traps
Running the hierarchy spec alone misses the real consumer import. A test-runner workaround would retain the shared-state leak.
